items.title: The hidden impact of cage position on behavioral phenotyping and reproducibility
items.summary: Documenting and controlling lifelong in-cage illumination differences by rack position in a neurobehavioral core (stated: uppermost vs lowermost shelves produced 70 vs 20 lx inside cages; cage position altered exploratory/risk-assessment behavior). Illumination was measured with a spot TES 1332 A digital lux meter (stated method).

people.name: Lior Bikovski
people.institution: Tel Aviv University (Myers Neuro-Behavioral Core Facility / Gray Faculty of Medical and Health Sciences), Tel-Aviv, Israel

people.name: Chaim G. Pick
people.institution: Tel Aviv University (Myers Neuro-Behavioral Core Facility / Gray Faculty of Medical and Health Sciences), Tel-Aviv, Israel

details.facts: Stated (full text, Scientific Reports, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0): male/female ICR mice housed from birth to adulthood on uppermost vs lowermost shelves of an IVC rack at Myers Neuro-Behavioral Core Facility (Tel Aviv University); in-cage light-phase illumination 70 lx (upper) vs 20 lx (lower) by TES 1332 A lux meter; lower-shelf mice left the light-dark box dark compartment faster (survived correction) and showed less EPM risk-assessment; locomotor activity, spatial memory, nociception, and optic-nerve diameter unchanged. Authors conclude cage position is a hidden confounder removable by counterbalancing. Corresponding datasets available from corresponding author on request.
details.inferences: Continuous in-cage light (and activity) logging with Hub Wheel with Hublink or Body Event Analysis Module 3 (BEAM3) could replace or supplement spot lux-meter checks and document developmental light exposure across many cages in a core facility. Equivalence of Hub light sensors to the TES 1332 A readings is untested. No purchasing intent or tooling gap is stated; the study is complete.
details.product_matches_raw: Hub Wheel with Hublink; Body Event Analysis Module 3 (BEAM3)
details.recommended_action: Human review; candidate for Hub Wheel/BEAM3 light-logging segment aimed at neurobehavioral cores that need to document rack-position illumination. No outreach from Scout.
details.review_note: Peer-reviewed Scientific Reports (OA CC BY-NC-ND); full text read for methods. Not in Outreach Log; no existing-relationship overlap. Key investigators not in Atlas; REQ-OPP-OPP-064 (Bikovski) and REQ-OPP-OPP-064-B (Pick) filed 2026-11-06. First authors Keidan/Sasonov appear trainee-level; not filed.

items.summary: Individual-animal home-cage palatable food intake measurement across weeks in group-housed mice (binge-like eating model, semaglutide treatment and discontinuation). Authors state that home-cage (22-h) intake was cage-level only (n = 4/cage), which precluded statistical comparison, and that future work should measure individual home-cage intake more precisely (stated limitation and future need).

people.name: Britny A. Hildebrandt
people.institution: University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine (Pittsburgh, PA)

people.name: Susanne E. Ahmari
people.institution: University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine (Pittsburgh, PA)

items.title: Standard touchscreen test procedures shift circadian rhythms in mice: a modified protocol to minimize circadian confounds
items.summary: Continuous home-cage circadian activity monitoring of mice undergoing daily operant/touchscreen testing, with control of chamber and home-cage lighting (stated method); authors state individual activity records were not available for pair-housed females because overhead PIR sensors give a cage-level aggregate (stated limitation).

details.facts: Stated (full text, bioRxiv preprint, CC BY-NC 4.0): Bussey-Saksida touchscreen chambers (Campden/Lafayette ABET II, Whisker); home-cage locomotor activity by overhead passive-infrared sensors with ClockLab (Actimetrics); standard screen light (~21 lux) caused ~3.5 h phase delay after 7 days of early-dark testing; 10 lighting conditions tested; recommendations include treating the chamber as a light source, brighter home-cage lighting, removing short-wavelength light, periodic DD probes. Limitations stated: pair-housed females lacked individual activity records (aggregate could mask one mouse shifting); bright home-cage light levels difficult to standardize.
details.inferences: Per-animal wearable movement plus proximity logging (Juxta) could give individual activity rhythms in pair-housed mice; Hub Wheel with Hublink logs wheel turns and in-cage light, which could document home-cage lux alongside rhythms; FED3/FED4 home-cage operant testing could be a low-light alternative to moving mice to touchscreen chambers (collaboration, not sales). Equivalence of these devices to PIR/ClockLab phase estimates is untested. No purchasing intent stated; lab already has PIR/ClockLab.
details.product_matches_raw: Juxta Social Proximity Loggers (Gen5); Hub Wheel with Hublink; Body Event Analysis Module 3 (BEAM3); FED3 (Feeding Experimentation Device 3); FED4 (Feeding Experimentation Device 4)
details.recommended_action: Human review; strong methods fit for circadian/operant segment (individual rhythms in pair housing, in-cage light logging, home-cage operant alternative via FED3/FED4). No outreach from Scout.
details.review_note: Preprint (not peer reviewed); open-license full text read for methods. Not in Outreach Log; no existing-relationship overlap. Key investigator not in Atlas; REQ-OPP-OPP-060 filed 2026-11-04. Co-author Ralph Mistlberger (SFU) is a senior circadian PI, not listed as key.

items.title: Voluntary exercise mitigates the effects of peri-adolescent social isolation on emotion recognition and the oxytocinergic system in male mice
items.summary: Chronic (12-week) home-cage voluntary wheel running in singly- vs group-housed mice, with running distance quantified across housing conditions (stated method).

details.facts: Stated (full text, Journal of Neuroendocrinology, CC BY-NC-ND, read via Europe PMC PMC13716504): weaned male C57BL/6J mice singly- or group-housed with an igloo or a Bio-Serv fast-track running wheel (Bioseb, France) for 12 weeks; wheel use checked as mean daily rotations per cage divided by mice per cage, collected at least 3 days/week over 4 weeks, converted to distance; individual running evaluated only in a 10-min test after 24 h deprivation. Isolation enhanced social investigation and impaired emotion discrimination and reduced PVN oxytocin neurons; exercise protected emotion discrimination and raised plasma OXT.
details.inferences: Continuous, wireless per-wheel logging (Hub Wheel with Hublink) could replace intermittent per-cage counts in this kind of chronic exercise x housing design; Juxta could add individual social-contact data in group-housed cages. items.title: NIH BRAIN BBQS Next-Generation Sensor Technology Development U01 (RFA-MH-26-140): final round June 15, 2027
items.summary: BBQS funds new sensors and bioelectronics that measure behavior in complex physical and social environments and synchronize those data with simultaneous neural recordings, in human and animal models. The NOFO names low or zero battery use, miniaturization, and wireless setups as key goals, which describes Juxta (wearable, month-long, proximity + motion + temperature) and the SFP (cage-floor foraging built to work with chronic neural recordings). June 15, 2027 is the last listed due date; the NOFO expires June 16, 2027. Awardees join a Research Consortium, so a behavioral-science PI partner is needed. Juxta6 and SFP are still in development; this would fund development, not a finished product.

details.hub_asset: Juxta (Gen5 / Juxta6) + Spatial Foraging Platform (in development) + Hublink
details.potential_value: NIMH and partners plan ~$10M for 6-8 awards per receipt date; budgets not capped; up to 5 years (per NOFO)
details.recommended_action: By Feb 2027: pick the asset (Juxta6 vs SFP), identify a WashU behavioral-neuroscience co-PI, and request an NIMH program-officer consult; decide go/no-go by March 2027

items.title: NSF DBI Infrastructure Innovation for Biological Research (NSF 23-578), Instrumentation area: field-behavior instrumentation
items.summary: The NSF BIO Innovation program funds new, significantly redesigned, or newly adapted instruments and methods with uses beyond one lab. Proposals are accepted anytime. ACORN (scheduled, logged, weatherproof playback) and Juxta (wearable social proximity logging) fit field ecology and animal-behavior research that NSF BIO supports and NIH usually doesn't. Matt's red squirrel and Kluane background gives a credible field-ecology use case. NSF BIO doesn't fund biomedical work, so the framing must be ecological and evolutionary. ACORN isn't shipping yet.

items.title: Wireless fleet data retrieval for the FED3 installed base
items.summary: FED3 logs to an on-board microSD card, so labs running many cages collect data by hand. The Hub's own Nov 2024 post estimates 100+ labs and 3,000+ FED3 devices. On FEDforum, users have built one-off Wi-Fi workarounds, and FED's developer called multi-device wireless harvesting 'not trivial'. Users also report university IT network restrictions that block ESP32 Wi-Fi devices. Hublink's BLE gateway sidesteps campus Wi-Fi, already has a FED3 integration path (ESP32-S3 Feather + SD backpack + multi-architecture FED3 library), and FED4 v1.7 lists optional Hublink BLE sync. Need is documented; willingness to pay for a retrofit or subscription is untested.

details.hub_asset: Hublink + FED3 (supported) + FED4 (in development, optional Hublink BLE sync)
details.potential_value: Strategic: a large installed base reachable through existing Hub software; possible retrofit kit or Hublink subscription revenue (amount unknown)
details.recommended_action: Count Hublink-connected FED3 users today, then decide whether to package a FED3-Hublink retrofit kit as a store SKU or wait for FED4 release; no external outreach until decided

items.title: Cage-scale programmable spatial foraging compatible with chronic neural recording
items.summary: Open naturalistic-foraging platforms are either room-scale or head-fixed. SWC's Aeon habitat is about 2.7 x 2.4 m with wheel-based foraging patches. Dynamic-foraging tasks such as Allen's are rig-based. FED3 offers single-location operant feeding in the home cage. No widely adopted tool appears to turn a standard home-cage floor into a distributed, programmable reward and cue field that works with chronic recordings, which is SFP's design. This is a hypothesis from a desk scan, not a validated gap: no user survey or demand data yet, and SFP is alpha stage and not for sale.
